newsitem.title: TURKEY: MENA seeks massive infrastructure financing.
newsitem.headline: MENA seeks massive infrastructure financing.

text.p: Middle Eastern and North Africa countries (MENA) said on Thursday massive infrastructure financing of up to $16 billion per year was needed over the next 10 to 15 years in order to see rapid growth in the region .

"Participants agreed that aiming at an improved growth performance in the region requires massive financing (of up to $16 billion per year over the next 10-15 years) in infrastructure as well as great improvements in efficiency," said a release at the end of an infrastructure conference co-sponsored by the World Bank and the European Commission.

It said the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development, the European Investment Bank and the International Finance Corporation as well as the sponsors stated their readiness to support this with both technical advice and finance.

Ministers from Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Tunisia, Turkey and the Palestinian Authority and an official delegation from Israel attended the three-day Private/Public Partnership in Infrastructure in the Middle East and North Africa conference.

"The conference has illustrated a broad consensus that the volume of investment required can only be achieved through a much higher inflow of private capital (in order of $3 billion per year at a minimum)...," the statement said.
It said attendants were willing to take the necessary policy steps to open infrastucture investments to a much higher degree of private participation.

"Governments' role was seen as crucial in ensuring the success of this evolution via setting targets, providing a clear and stable policy framework, setting standards for services, encouraging and regulating competition and ensuing arbitration," it added.
